title: benchmark-lab: add autoscaling load generator + reporting pipeline
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Add a horizontally autoscaling load generator and a reporting pipeline to consolidate benchmark lab results into the observability metrics store. This enables realistic representative workload runs under autoscaled serving capacity and provides per-variant reporting for profiling baselines and regression detection.

What this PR does: - New load generator service (benchmark-lab/loadgen/autoscaler) that drives representative workload runners (chat, streaming, embeddings) and adjusts concurrency using the same autoscaling signals used by Dedicated autoscale policies. - Reporting pipeline (benchmark-lab/reporting) that ingests run artifacts, computes latency/throughput/percentiles and KV-cache hit metrics, and exports to metrics-db and a reporting S3 bucket. - Adds GitHub Actions workflow to schedule nightly mixed-workload runs and publish baseline reports. - End-to-end integration with perf-canary for canarying new kernel/quantization profiles.

Checklist: - [x] Implement load generator and autoscaling policy adapter - [x] Representative workload runners updated to emit structured run metadata - [x] Reporting DAG, aggregation, and S3 export implemented - [x] Nightly CI workflow + permissions - [x] Unit + integration tests covering loadgen and reporting ingestion - [x] Update docs and runbook for interpreting baselines

Notes and design choices: - Autoscaler uses the same signal set (tokens/s, p95 latency) as Dedicated autoscale controller to mimic production behaviour; tuning knobs are exposed via config and default to conservative ramp rates to avoid noisy bursts. - Reporting pipeline aggregates both raw token traces and summarized metrics; raw traces are retained for 30 days to support profiling needs. - To reduce cost, the load generator supports prefix/KV caching warmups to recreate steady-state cache hit rates before measurement windows.

Related: ENG-4217 (design), ENG-4290 (reporting schema), SUP-1123 (customer request for autoscale benchmarks)

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Could you explain the decision to reuse Dedicated autoscaler signals rather than a synthetic load-specific metric? Concern is that production fluctuations may introduce noise into baselines.

Maya Chen: Replied: Reusing the Dedicated signals ensures the load generator exercises the same scaling boundaries as customers see in production. We add a warmup window and a 5-minute stabilization period before measurements to reduce noise.
Priya Natarajan: Please add schema versioning to the reporting output so future changes don't break downstream dashboards.
Maya Chen: Added schema/v1.yaml and a compatibility doc in the reporting folder. Also added an integration test that validates schema compliance.
Samir Patel: CI failed on the first run due to IAM permission to write to the reporting bucket; added a GH action step to acquire short-lived creds in the workflow. Approving after green CI.
release_notes: Add autoscaling load generator and reporting pipeline for benchmark lab. Enables nightly representative runs, autoscale-aware workloads, and consolidated baseline reporting.
notes_for_ops: Grant the GitHub Actions runner write access to metrics-db and reporting S3. Monitor p95 latency drift; rollback policy defined in runbook.
stability_impact: low: defaults use conservative autoscale ramping; however enablement of nightly runs will increase cluster load by scheduled windows.
